newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt seeks stake in other airport authorities.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt seeks stake in other airport authorities.

text.p: Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG), owner and manager of Frankfurt Airport, said it is seeking financial stakes in German and foreign airport authorities.
FAG chairman Wilhelm Bender said the company wanted talks with Cologne airport on operational co-operation and was also interested in other domestic and foreign strategic financial shareholdings.
FAG had extensive know-how in airport management, passenger and cargo handling, baggage operations and other fields, he added at a news conference.
The company already offers handling services at six Spanish airports and is a partner in the new Athens airport consortium, he pointed out.
FAG would earn 90 million of its 2.4 billion marks turnover from shareholdings this year, he added.
"This does not mean we want to rule the German airport landscape but this company can make large contributions to the changing airport scene," Bender said.
At Saarbruecken, FAG would take a 51 percent stake in the airport operating company in 1997 and will be responsible for the entire airport management, Bender said.
Cologne was of interest since the federal government was thinking of selling its stake and a new high-speed rail link would link the two airports from 2001.
"I could imagine successful activities in Frankfurt could also be operated by us there," Bender said.
"Cologne, for example, is the second-largest cargo airport in Germany and there are possible areas of co-operation," he added.
But stakes would be taken for financial and not operational reasons despite Frankfurt's present loss of traffic to other European hubs, Bender stressed.
"Of course we want to avoid the traffic loss which we see out of North Rhine Westphalia to Amsterdam in everyday business."
But he added: "We do not want to have these stakes to ensure traffic for Frankfurt but to make profits."

The ownership of German airports resulted from the country's federal structure and was not market-orientated in contrast to London or Paris, he said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
